evidence.label: The irrationality exponent of pi is 2
Lean doc (main theorem formalized)
evidence.note: Lean formalization of the main theorem (exponent equals 2); the Flint–Hills consequence is outside the formalized statement.

headline: Fractions can never get unusually close to π.
scope: The result is about π only. It does not cover other constants.
plain: Every number can be approached by fractions. For most numbers, the closest fractions miss by about 1 divided by the square of their bottom number. This paper claims to prove that π behaves like most numbers. No fraction gets much closer to π than that rule allows.
doesNot: This does not prove that π is irrational or transcendental. Those facts were proved in the 1760s and in 1882.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.significanceWhy: It ends a 73-year chain of better and better limits on a famous constant.

visual.title: Best proven limit on π’s irrationality exponent
visual.note: Smaller is better. 2 is the lowest possible value.

sections.title: The story
sections.body: In 1953, Kurt Mahler proved that the irrationality exponent (a score for how closely fractions can approximate a number) of π is at most 42. Since then, mathematicians made this limit smaller step by step. Salikhov reached about 7.61 in 2008, and Zeilberger and Zudilin about 7.10 in 2020. In September 2026, two weeks before this paper, Yufei Bai trimmed it to about 7.102. Most experts expected the true value to be 2, but no one could prove it.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: A value of 2 means π is not special in this way. The paper also settles a well-known puzzle: the Flint Hills series, the sum of 1 / (n³ sin²n). Alekseyev showed in 2011 that whether this sum converges (approaches a fixed value) is tied to π's irrationality exponent, with the dividing line at 2.5. An exponent of 2 is below that line, so the sum converges.

sections.title: Where it leads
sections.body: The same methods could apply to other constants, such as log 2 or ζ(3), where the known limits are still far above 2. This is one of 10 results with a published reasoning summary, so mathematicians can study how the model found the proof.

sections.title: What it says about AI
sections.body: Strong human experts worked on this problem for decades. If the proof holds, it shows that AI can finish a long line of human work on a classical question. The main theorem has a Lean formalization listed, a computer-checkable version of the statement and proof, but the Flint–Hills part is not covered.

hypeCheck: Major if the proof holds. The main theorem has a Lean formalization listed, but the Flint–Hills step is not machine-checked and specialists have not yet published a review.

glossary.meaning: A number that is not a fraction of two whole numbers, like π.
A score for how closely fractions can approximate a number. The lowest possible score is 2.
When the sum of an endless list of numbers approaches a fixed value.
